eligibility_criteria.value: For individuals and families with low or no income.
California residency.
Citizenship or qualified non-citizen status.
Income and resource thresholds.
Social Security Number.
A CalFresh household is a group of people who purchase and prepare food together.

California does not provide CalFresh to ineligible noncitizens, including those who are undocumented. The California Food Assistance Program (CFAP) provides similar state-funded food benefits to certain lawfully present noncitizens who are not eligible for federal CalFresh.

Gross monthly income limits by household size: 1 person $2,610; 2 people $3,526; 3 people $4,442; 4 people $5,360; 5 people $6,276; 6 people $7,192; 7 people $8,110; 8 people $9,026; each additional member +$918.

Households with someone who is 60 or older or disabled may qualify even if their income is higher than the gross income limit; they only need to meet the net income limit. Households with no members who are 60 or older or disabled must meet both the gross income limit and the net income limit.

Individuals and families including U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents (green card holders), and noncitizens with certain immigration statuses may be eligible. Starting April 1, 2026, fewer noncitizens are eligible for CalFresh.

Expedited Services (ES) is available to certain applicants; if eligible, the application must be processed within three (3) days of the CalFresh application date. ES may apply if the applicant's identity can be verified AND one of the following is met: (a) household monthly gross income is less than $150.00 and liquid resources are $100.00 or less; (b) household combined monthly gross income and liquid resources are less than combined monthly rent/mortgage and utility expenses; (c) applicant is a migrant or seasonal worker with $100.00 or less in liquid resources.

As of June 1, 2026, the CalFresh work and community engagement requirements apply to people who are between the ages of 18 and 64, do not have a disability, and do not live with a CalFresh household member under 14 years old. Some people may be excused.

People subject to the ABAWD work requirement can only get 3 full months of CalFresh benefits every 3 years, unless they work an average of 20 hours a week, are in school or job training for 20 hours a week of class time or at least half-time, volunteer, are excused, or live in a county where the requirement is waived.

A person is excused from the ABAWD work requirement if they live in a CalFresh household with a CalFresh household member under age 14 (other exemptions also exist, e.g. under 18 or over 64, pregnancy, health conditions).

General CalFresh work requirements (work registration) apply to people ages 16 to 59 who are able to work: take a suitable job if offered and do not voluntarily quit or reduce hours below 30 per week without good reason. Excused if, among others: younger than 16 or 60+; caring for a dependent child under 6 or a person with a disability; earning at least $217.50 a week before taxes or working 30+ hours a week; getting or applying for unemployment benefits; disabled; at least half-time in school or training; meeting another program's work rules (e.g. CalWORKs); in a drug or alcohol treatment program.

Sacramento County is not listed among the counties where the ABAWD work requirement is waived (Nov 1, 2025 to Oct 31, 2026: Alpine, Colusa, Imperial, Merced, Monterey, Plumas, Tulare; Nov 1, 2026 to Oct 31, 2027: Colusa, Imperial, Kings, Merced, Monterey, Plumas, Tulare).
Starting June 1, 2026, college students are eligible for CalFresh through Local Programs that Increase Employability (LPIE).
To keep benefits: the SAR 7 (semi-annual report) is due by the 5th of the month. It can be completed online at BenefitsCal.com, or the form can be submitted by mail or in person.
To keep benefits: many households must complete a SAR 7 six (6) months after applying.
To keep benefits: in California, most households are on a 12-month certification period (renewal). Households where everyone is 60 or older or has a disability can be certified for 24 months.

required_documents.value: Documents are not required to submit an application. The county will say what needs to be provided, and documents can be uploaded later on BenefitsCal.
Identity of applicant: birth certificate, driver's license, paycheck, voter registration card, school records, or U.S. passport.
Social Security Numbers: Social Security card, or proof of application if no SSN exists.

Immigration status (if applicable): immigration papers/forms/cards (copy of both sides), certificate of naturalization, or other proof from USCIS such as work authorization or a letter of decision. All are verified through SAVE; the I-688 is not acceptable.
Residence: driver's license, check stub, rent or mortgage receipt, or utility bill.
Money you earn: dated check stubs for the last 30 days, statement from your employer, or copy of last year's tax return.
Vehicle registration: DMV registration certificate.
Other income: a current benefit check, copies of child support or alimony checks, award letters, or statement from a college financial aid office.
Resources: bank statements (savings and checking), mortgage statements, life insurance policies, statements of stocks, bonds or CDs.
Housing and other bills: mortgage or rent receipts, lease or statement from your landlord, property tax statement, utility bills.
Medical bills (only for household members aged 60+ or permanently disabled): billing statement or itemized receipts.
Childcare: receipts showing amount, date paid, name of person care was for, and provider signature and date.

application_method.value: Apply by mail: P.O. Box 487, Sacramento, CA 95812.
Apply in person at a Sacramento County DHA office location.

Minimum required to file an application: applicant's name; household's address (unless homeless); and signature of the head of household, any adult household member, an authorized representative, or a responsible minor. The county encourages completing as much of the application as possible to minimize delays.
Paper application forms CF 285, CF 485 and SAWS 2 PLUS are available in English, Spanish and Russian; other languages are on the CDSS website.
BenefitsCal steps: (1) fill in and submit the application; (2) upload documents; (3) the county reviews the application; (4) the county contacts the applicant to schedule an interview.

processing_time.value: Eligible households that complete the initial application process must be given an opportunity to participate as soon as possible, but not later than 30 calendar days after the application was filed (CalFresh Manual of Policies and Procedures, Division 63, Sections 63-300 to 63-301). In emergency situations, Expedited CalFresh benefits may be received no later than the 3rd calendar day after the application is filed (Saturday and Sunday count as 1 day).

eligibility_criteria.value: Have a Social Security number, or have authorization to work in the United States (if not a US citizen).
Have earned enough wages during the base period.
Be fully or partially unemployed.
Be unemployed through no fault of your own.
Be physically able and available to work.
Be looking for work each week.
Be ready and willing to accept work right away.
All claims have a one-week, unpaid, waiting period.
To keep receiving benefits, you must certify for benefits every two weeks.

required_documents.value: Name (including all names used while working) and Social Security number.
Mailing and residence address (if different) and phone number.
Last employer's complete name, address (mailing and physical location), and phone number.
Last day worked and the reason you're no longer working (laid off, quit, fired, or left work because of a trade dispute).
Work history during the 18 months prior to applying, including out-of-state employment: all employers' names, dates employed, and wages earned.
State-issued driver license number or identification card number.

Citizenship status and whether you have the legal right to work in the United States; if authorized to work through USCIS, the title of the employment authorization document and information from it (such as Alien Registration Number, card number, expiration date).

application_method.value: Apply online through myEDD (UI Online), which EDD describes as the fastest and most convenient way to apply for unemployment and manage a claim.
You must be at least 18 years old to apply online; applicants under 18 can apply by phone, fax, or mail.
You may apply for benefits as soon as you are unemployed or your hours are reduced.

eligibility_criteria.value: There are not enough resources for everyone; the Coordinated Access System focuses on making sure those most at risk are served first.

evidence_records.claim_value: Sacramento Coordinated Access System: call 2-1-1 and press 8 for shelter, housing and other homelessness services, including homelessness prevention. A specialist works to determine availability and eligibility.
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: Access route, not a single fund. TD 20.3: describe the 211 referral process; never claim to reserve a slot.

evidence_records.claim_value: Sacramento Steps Forward (Continuum of Care lead agency) with 2-1-1 Sacramento; 2-1-1 schedules appointments with approved Problem Solving Access Point (PSAP) agencies.
evidence_records.source_title: Homelessness Prevention in Sacramento | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Sept 10, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: SSF states it is not a direct provider of housing resources or shelters.

evidence_records.claim_value: Sacramento County
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)

evidence_records.claim_value: There are not enough resources for everyone; the Coordinated Access System focuses on making sure those most at risk are served first.
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: No program-specific eligibility rules are published.

evidence_records.claim_value: Financial assistance through problem-solving services is limited and must directly lead to securing housing.
evidence_records.source_title: The Coordinated Access System | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 6, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: v0.3: replaces the v0.2 wording from the general prevention page, which was too vague to verify.

evidence_records.claim_value: Call 2-1-1 and press 8. 2-1-1 assesses the needs and circumstances of callers and schedules appointments with approved PSAP agencies.
evidence_records.source_title: Homelessness Prevention in Sacramento | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Sept 10, 2026)

evidence_records.claim_value: Toll-free: 1-844-546-1464. If 2-1-1 is hard to reach: 916-498-1000, still pressing 8.
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)

evidence_records.claim_value: Coordinated Access hours: Monday through Saturday, 7:00 a.m. to 7:00 p.m.
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: 2-1-1 Sacramento's general referral line is listed as 24/7; the press-8 Coordinated Access line has the hours shown here. Another SSF page says CAS hours were updated starting October 1; this page (modified Oct 12, 2026) is the newer source.

evidence_records.claim_value: 2-1-1 Sacramento: text your ZIP code to 898-211, or use the online chat.
evidence_records.source_title: Housing Resources | 2-1-1 Sacramento
evidence_records.notes: General 2-1-1 referral channel (discovery source).

evidence_records.claim_value: The Coordinated Access line is published as operating: call 2-1-1 and press 8 (or 1-844-546-1464), Monday through Saturday, 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.
evidence_records.source_title: Access Support: Get Help with Homelessness | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 12, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: Basis for availability = confirmed_open: the access route is accepting calls (TD 9.2: published status only, not proof of funding or capacity). Funding context: the Sacramento CoC's state HHAP allocations include $2 million annually dedicated to keeping households housed through prevention efforts (SSF HHAP page, expenditures current through July 31, 2026: https://www.sacramentostepsforward.org/provider-hub/homeless-housing-assistance-and-prevention-hhap-grants/). Help for any one household is not guaranteed.

evidence_records.claim_value: Anyone at risk of or experiencing homelessness, or who is fleeing or attempting to flee domestic violence, sexual assault, or human trafficking, and meets income requirements, is eligible for problem-solving services.
evidence_records.source_title: The Coordinated Access System | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 6, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: Answer to 'What makes someone eligible for a problem-solving access point (PSAP) referral?'. Income limits are not published; unknown income is not a mismatch.

evidence_records.claim_value: Additional verification documents (proof of income, eviction filings, etc.) are required for financial assistance.
evidence_records.source_title: The Coordinated Access System | Sacramento Steps Forward (page last modified Oct 6, 2026)
evidence_records.notes: Not needed just to call 2-1-1; needed if financial assistance is offered.
